Specify quasi-identifier values that vary by row

Source: R/anon_risk.R
anon_quasi_values.Rd

Describes how to take one value per subject from a long dataset, such as a findings domain, for use in anon_risk(). For each test code in tests, the first non-missing, non-blank result_col value per subject (in row order, after filter) becomes a quasi-identifier. Only that value is measured; other rows for the same test identify the subject just as well, so they need the same treatment before data is shared.

Usage

anon_quasi_values(
  dataset,
  test_col,
  tests,
  result_col,
  filter = NULL,
  names = tests
)

Arguments

dataset

Name of the dataset in the list passed to anon_risk().

test_col

Name of the column holding test codes (e.g. "VSTESTCD").

tests

Test codes to use (e.g. c("HEIGHT", "WEIGHT")).

result_col

Name of the column holding the result (e.g. "VSSTRESN").

filter

Optional one-sided formula evaluated in the dataset to select rows, e.g. ~ VSBLFL == "Y" for baseline values. Variables not found in the dataset are looked up where the formula was created. It must return TRUE or FALSE for each row. It applies to every test in tests; use separate specifications when tests need different filters (for example, height recorded once at screening without a baseline flag). A warning is given when a test has no values.

names

Names for the resulting quasi-identifiers. Defaults to tests.

Value

An object of class "anon_quasi_values".

Examples

anon_quasi_values("vs", "VSTESTCD", c("HEIGHT", "WEIGHT"), "VSSTRESN",
                  filter = ~ VSBLFL == "Y")
#> Quasi-identifier values from `vs`: HEIGHT = first non-missing VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD == "HEIGHT"; WEIGHT = first non-missing VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD == "WEIGHT"
#> Filter: VSBLFL == "Y"
